ideas.description: Exploit: a booster that leaves the training trajectory unchanged. It replaces I064 with a paired design that has no trajectory noise. On the E036 tip, at the end of train() and after the final Lookahead copy (which lerps BN running_mean/var from different fast weights and never recomputes them): reset every BN layer's running stats, set momentum=None (cumulative average), run a no-grad train-mode forward at 32 px over K batches of 2000 training images with the usual crop and flip, then restore momentum. Capture this forward-only graph in build on synthetic channels_last tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Eval stays a plain forward pass. Judge it with an offline instrumented copy on unselected seeds 13–32. In each trial, evaluate the averaged model once before recalibration and once after, so the two numbers share the exact same trained weights and the difference has no trajectory or rebuild noise. Do the same for K=1 and K=3. Commit the better K, then run ar.py to get time and the seeds 0–2 check. The submission evaluates only once.
ideas.expected: Time rises 0.02–0.05 s (+0.4–1%, to about 5.33–5.36 s). The paired gain per seed should fall between −0.05 and +0.2 pp, median about +0.05. Keep if the mean paired gain is at least +0.05 pp (break-even against the ~1.5 s/pp dial for ≤0.05 s) and positive in at least 13 of 20 seeds. A gain of ≥0.15 pp supports H1.3.6 and pays for about 0.35 epoch of trimming. A gain of ≤0 refutes it: Lookahead's resets every 5 steps already keep the BN stats consistent, which closes the search for a booster that leaves the trajectory unchanged (W3/W6 crux).

ideas.description: Explore/booster, the step-count crux (W3, W5). E041 found that removing early 20 px steps cost as much as a uniform trim. That suggests early accuracy is carried by optimizer steps, not by pixels. On the E036 tip, use batch 1000 instead of 2000 only during the 20 px phase (the first 30% of data passes, so about 69 steps become about 138). Same data and same pixels; only the step count and per-step overhead change. Key the LR triangle, the whitening-bias detach (20%) and the resolution switch to data progress (samples seen), so they land at the same data point. In this phase, scale the SGD-group lr linearly (×0.5) and keep the Muon lr per step unchanged. Lookahead stays every 5 steps; alpha is near 0 this early. From 24 px on, batch 2000 is unchanged, so the 24/28/32 phases, freeze and Lookahead tail are identical. Capture batch-1000 graphs at 20 px, both the full and whitening-detached variants, in build with channels_last tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against E036 on the same seeds (reuse E038's 13–22 and run E036 once on 23–32; the C/D/selection ideas share this baseline), plus seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: Time rises 0.05–0.12 s (+1–2.5%), from about 69 extra 20 px steps at roughly 1–1.5 ms of overhead each plus lower kernel efficiency at batch 1000. The held-out 20-seed mean should move between 0 and +0.3 pp, median about +0.1. A gain of ≥0.15 pp supports H5.2 and is a better booster than epochs (≥1.5 pp per s). It would also fund E040/E041-style early trims. A change of ≤+0.05 pp refutes the step-count reading: E041's cost then came from compressing the LR schedule, and early batch size is a dead lever (which also settles H5.1.3/H5.2.1 without running them).

ideas.description: Explore, the batch-size crux named by W2, W5 and W6. On the E036 tip at the same true epoch count (9.25), lower the batch from 2000 to 1500 everywhere: 33 steps per epoch with the ragged batch dropped, so about 308 steps instead of 231. Scale the SGD-group lr linearly (×0.75). Muon lr per step and momentum 0.6 stay unchanged. The resolution phases, LR triangle, Lookahead ramp (still every 5 steps), whitening detach (20%) and group-1 freeze (75%) stay as fractions of the new step count. Recapture every resolution and variant at batch 1500 in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against E036 on the same seeds, plus seeds 0–2. Hiverge's record uses 1536 under Muon. I026 (1250, older base) was vetoed, but E041 has since shown that steps carry accuracy.
ideas.expected: Time rises 0.15–0.30 s (+3–6%, to about 5.5–5.6 s), from 77 extra steps of fixed overhead plus lower tile efficiency. The held-out mean should move between −0.1 and +0.4 pp, median about +0.15. The change is net positive if the gain is at least Δtime/1.5 s/pp (≈0.15 pp for +0.22 s); a trim can then cash it in. A gain under 0.1 pp means batch 2000 is at or below the useful critical batch, which closes H5.1 toward smaller batches.

ideas.description: Exploit, staggered FreezeOut cascade. This is the only remaining backward-truncation lever that targets the largest block, group 2 (~51% of conv MACs). On the E036 tip, put the group-2 conv filters (Muon) and group-2 BN params (SGD) in their own param groups. Their LR follows the global schedule until 75%, then decays linearly to 0 by 90% of steps; E028's annealed freeze is what kept group 1 neutral. For the last 10% of steps (about 23 steps, 32 px, group 1 already frozen), detach group 2's output before group 3 and use a new compiled 32 px step with no group-1/2 backward and no update for those params. Group-2 BN stays in train mode, and Lookahead still averages every param. Capture the new variant in build with channels_last tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against E036 on the same seeds, plus seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: Time falls 0.12–0.20 s (−2.5 to −4%, to about 5.12–5.2 s), since group-2 wgrad and dgrad are about 30% of a frozen 32 px step. The held-out mean should move between −0.3 and 0 pp, median about −0.1. Supports H2.6.8 if the loss is ≤0.1 pp, a rate of ≥1.5 s/pp that beats the epoch dial. It can then be stacked with a booster (BN recalibration or early small batch) to get back over the bar. A loss of ≥0.2 pp means the deep features still move usefully during the averaging window, and the cascade stops at group 1.

ideas.description: Explore diagnostic, with no recipe change. It replaces I058 and adds the overhead accounting from W5's crux. Offline, on the E036 tip with synthetic channels_last data at batch 2000: (1) torch.profiler traces of the compiled 32 px full step, the whitening-detached step, the frozen step and the 20/24 px steps. Record GPU time by kernel class (conv fwd/dgrad/wgrad, BN, GELU, pool, elementwise, Muon NS, Lookahead) and by layer, plus achieved TFLOP/s per conv. Explicitly compare group-1 conv1 (Cin=24, 31×31) against the group-2 convs. (2) One trace of a whole timed train() for seed 13 on real data. Record GPU idle fraction, per-epoch augmentation/interpolate/permute time, and time outside the step graphs. Write the table to the notebook, and label each kept lever as compute-bound or bandwidth-bound (H4.3). Do not edit submissions/arena/.
ideas.expected: Time and accuracy are unchanged. Predictions: GPU idle plus non-step work under 5% of train time; non-GEMM kernels at least 30% of a 32 px full step (H6.3.1); conv1 below half of group-2 TFLOP/s with about 50% probability (H6.4.1); 24 px layer-weighted throughput within 20% of 32 px (H6.1.1 likely refuted). Decision rules: if conv1 is under half of group-2 efficiency and at least 10% of step time, raise the Cin-padding idea (H6.4.2) to priority 4. If idle plus augmentation is over 5%, queue a systems fix. Otherwise close H6's systems branch, leaving step count and backward truncation as the only levers.

ideas.description: Exploit, a milder dose of the E031 near-miss. E031's top-90% selection cost −0.27 pp for −0.63 s (~2.3 s/pp, nominally better than the dial but within noise). On the E036 tip, return per-sample losses from the compiled step (reduction='none', then mean for backward) and scatter them into a GPU buffer indexed by sample id, created and reset in prepare. From epoch 2 on, each epoch's shuffle uses only the 95% of samples with the highest loss in the previous pass (topk on the GPU), with batch 2000 and the ragged batch dropped. Total steps fall from about 231 to about 220. The resolution phases, LR triangle, Lookahead, whitening detach and freeze stay as fractions of the new step count. Warm up the modified step variants in build, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on seeds 13–32 against E036 on the same seeds, plus seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: Time falls 0.2–0.28 s (−4 to −5%, to about 5.05–5.1 s). A uniform cut of the same steps costs about 0.15–0.18 pp on the dial. The held-out mean should move between −0.25 and 0 pp, median about −0.12. A loss of ≤0.1 pp supports H2.7.1 (selection beats a uniform trim) and makes it stackable with a booster. A loss of ≥0.18 pp means selection is no better than the dial, which closes H2.7.

ideas.description: Exploit, systems only, with identical math. On the E036 tip, widen the frozen whitening conv's output from 24 to 32 channels with 8 zero filters and a zero, detached bias. Widen group-1 conv1's input to 32 channels, with zero weights on the 8 new input channels. Initialize at the original shape first, then pad, so RNG consumption is unchanged. Under Muon, those columns stay exactly zero: their gradient is zero, NS left-multiplication keeps zero columns zero, and norms and wd are unaffected. GELU(0)=0 keeps the padded activations zero. Eval uses the padded net. Before launching, check offline that the padded and unpadded forward outputs match (allclose in fp16) on the same weights, and that the padded weights stay exactly 0 after 20 training steps. Recapture every graph in build, with error_on_recompile on. Best run after the profiling diagnostic; raise priority if it shows conv1 is inefficient.
ideas.expected: Time changes by −2% to +1%. Cin=24 is already a multiple of 8, so the alignment gain may not cover conv1's +33% FLOPs in fwd/wgrad. Accuracy should stay within rebuild noise (3-seed mean within 0.1 pp; per-seed shifts up to ~0.3 pp from kernel reselection). A time cut of ≥2% supports H6.4.2 and comes at no accuracy cost, which matters at zero margin. Under 1% refutes it, and the misaligned channel count is not the stem cost.

drop.reason: Replaced by the paired BN-recalibration idea (H1.3.6). Evaluating before and after recalibration in the same process removes trajectory and rebuild noise, so the ~0.05 pp effect the committee forecasts becomes measurable. The old design (unpaired seeds 3–12, gate ≥0.15 pp) could not separate it.

The committee agrees (0 improve votes, ~−0.07 s, −0.1 to −0.2 pp expected). E040/E041 show early steps and phase jumps are not free, and saving ~0.07 s for ≥0.1 pp (~0.7 s/pp) is far worse than the epoch dial. Likely dominated.

Replaced by a sharper profiling diagnostic (H6.4.1). It adds the whole-train idle and augmentation accounting from W5's crux and an explicit conv1-vs-group-2 efficiency test, with decision rules that gate the Cin-padding idea. The committee's 0.4 conflict was about time forecasts for a diagnostic, which is not informative.

structured_output.summary:
Where things stand: the E036 tip runs in 5.31 s. Its true mean accuracy is about 0.754 (0.7538 on fresh seeds), so it clears the 0.753 local bar only about 55–70% of the time. Any further time cut therefore needs an accuracy gain to pay for it, and should beat the epoch dial of about 1.5 s per pp of accuracy.

**Accuracy boosters (to pay for cuts):**
- **BN recalibration (H1.3.6), priority 4.** It replaces I064. The test is now paired inside one process: each trial is evaluated before and after recalibration on the same trained weights. That removes trajectory and rebuild noise, so the ~0.05 pp the committee forecasts can actually be measured. It costs about 0.03 s, so a gain of +0.05 pp already breaks even.
- **Batch 1000 only in the 20 px phase (H5.2), priority 4.** This tests the step-count crux that E041 raised: it adds steps at the cheapest resolution for about +0.1 s.
- **Global batch 1500 (H5.1.2), priority 3.** This is the crux named by W2, W5 and W6.

**Time cuts to stack once accuracy is paid for:**
- **Freeze group 2 for the last 10% of steps (H2.6.8), priority 3.** About −0.15 s; group 2 is the largest block.
- **Keep the top 95% of samples by loss (H2.7.1), priority 2.** A milder dose of E031's near-miss.
- **Pad the stem's 24 channels to 32 (H6.4.2), priority 2.** The math is unchanged, so it has no accuracy cost.

**Diagnostic:** a sharpened profiling run (H6.4.1, priority 3) replaces I058. It adds GPU idle and augmentation accounting over a whole run, and its result decides whether the padding idea moves up.

**Dropped:**
- I065 (16 px start): the committee expects it to trade worse than the dial.
- I058 and I064: replaced by the sharper versions above.

**Not queued:**
- Freezing at 70–71%: it saves only about 0.09 s, and a difference that small can't be resolved with 20 seeds.
- Re-testing E040 on fresh seeds: even the optimistic reading only matches the dial, and its seeds 0–2 already miss the bar.

**Evaluation protocol:**
- New ideas are judged on seeds 13–32 against E036 on the same seeds. E038's seeds 13–22 are reused, and E036 is run once on 23–32 to complete the baseline.
- Final validation must use seeds 33 and up, because 13–32 will now be used for selection.
- I062 is still running. Its result says where E037's freeze cliff comes from.
